notes.text: Oxygen devices named for 93225: simple face mask (Hudson mask), Venturi mask and non-rebreather mask. Managing oxygen therapy with these devices is also a core clinical skill assessed in the labs.
Tutorial doctor's notes (asthma): give O2 if SpO2 on pulse oximetry is less than 92% (adults) or 95% (children).

Life-threatening acute asthma (Australian Asthma Handbook figure): use oxygen to drive the nebuliser (piped oxygen or a cylinder with a high-flow regulator, 6 L/min). Children: maintain SaO2 of at least 95%. Adults: titrate oxygen to a target SaO2 of 93-95%.
Examples of oxygen orders in the case studies: Trent (pneumonia) O2 via nasal prongs at 4 L/min; Sarah (COPD) 2 L nasal prongs, after arriving with SpO2 87-88% on 6 L via Hudson mask.
